Pick a door. The host — who knows what's behind every door — opens every other door but one, always revealing a goat, never the car. Do you stay with your original pick, or switch to the one door the host left closed? Play a few rounds yourself, then use the simulate buttons to run thousands of rounds instantly and watch the win rates settle exactly where the math predicts.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// VM is the shared utility library, loaded globally via _includes/head-scripts.html (js/**). This page uses VM.ui.renderTable.
VM = window.VM
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// newGame: deals a fresh round for the given door count — a random car
// door and the phase reset to "pick". Nothing is opened until the player
// picks (see openHostDoors), matching how the real game show works:
// the host only reveals goats after you've committed to an initial choice.
function newGame(doorCount) {
  return {
    doorCount,
    carDoor: Math.floor(Math.random() * doorCount),
    phase: "pick",
    pickedDoor: null,
    openedDoors: [],
    remainingDoor: null,
    decision: null,
    won: null
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// openHostDoors: the host opens every goat door except the picked door and
// one other, leaving exactly two doors closed no matter how many doors the
// game started with — the pick, and this "remaining" door. If the pick
// itself is the car, the host has doorCount - 1 goats to choose from and
// picks which one stays closed uniformly at random; if the pick is a goat,
// the car is the only door the host can't open, so it's forced to be the
// remaining door. This is the standard generalization of the classic
// 3-door problem to N doors.
function openHostDoors(doorCount, carDoor, pickedDoor) {
  const otherGoats = []
  for (let i = 0; i < doorCount; i++) {
    if (i !== pickedDoor && i !== carDoor) otherGoats.push(i)
  }

  let remainingDoor
  if (pickedDoor === carDoor) {
    remainingDoor = otherGoats[Math.floor(Math.random() * otherGoats.length)]
  } else {
    remainingDoor = carDoor
  }

  const openedDoors = []
  for (let i = 0; i < doorCount; i++) {
    if (i !== pickedDoor && i !== remainingDoor) openedDoors.push(i)
  }

  return {openedDoors, remainingDoor}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// simulateRound: plays one full round with a fixed strategy end to end, no
// UI involved — used by the "simulate more rounds" buttons to generate
// many instant trials for the law-of-large-numbers convergence plot.
function simulateRound(doorCount, strategy) {
  const carDoor = Math.floor(Math.random() * doorCount)
  const pickedDoor = Math.floor(Math.random() * doorCount)
  const {remainingDoor} = openHostDoors(doorCount, carDoor, pickedDoor)
  const finalDoor = strategy === "switch" ? remainingDoor : pickedDoor
  return {doorCount, pickedDoor, carDoor, decision: strategy, won: finalDoor === carDoor, source: "simulated"}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// formatPct: win rates are 0/0 before any rounds of a given strategy have
// been played — guard against rendering "NaN%".
function formatPct(wins, total) {
  if (total === 0) return "—"
  return ((wins / total) * 100).toFixed(1) + "%"
}
```

//| output: false

```{ojs}
// doorRow: renders the doors themselves as clickable tiles. Rebuilt fresh
// on every gameState change (like drawDiagnosticCanvas on the Bayes' page)
// rather than patched in place — there's no zoom/pan state worth
// preserving on a button grid the way there is on a Plotly chart.
//
// Click handlers read/write `mutable gameState` (not the bare `gameState`
// reference used for rendering above) so they always act on the live
// current state, even though the handler itself was created back when this
// cell last ran — this is the standard Observable pattern for widgets that
// mutate their own state from a DOM event.
doorRow = {
  const state = gameState
  const container = document.createElement("div")
  container.className = "monty-hall-doors"

  for (let i = 0; i < state.doorCount; i++) {
    const doorEl = document.createElement("button")
    doorEl.type = "button"
    doorEl.className = "monty-hall-door"

    const isOpened = state.openedDoors.includes(i)
    const isPicked = state.pickedDoor === i
    const isRemaining = state.remainingDoor === i
    const showResult = state.phase === "result"

    let icon = "🚪"
    if (isOpened) {
      icon = "🐐"
      doorEl.classList.add("monty-hall-door-goat")
    } else if (showResult) {
      icon = i === state.carDoor ? "🚗" : "🐐"
      doorEl.classList.add(i === state.carDoor ? "monty-hall-door-car" : "monty-hall-door-goat")
    }

    if (isPicked) doorEl.classList.add("monty-hall-door-picked")
    if (isRemaining && state.phase !== "pick") doorEl.classList.add("monty-hall-door-remaining")

    doorEl.innerHTML = `<span class="monty-hall-door-icon">${icon}</span><span class="monty-hall-door-label">Door ${i + 1}</span>`
    doorEl.disabled = state.phase !== "pick"

    doorEl.onclick = () => {
      const current = mutable gameState
      if (current.phase !== "pick") return
      const {openedDoors, remainingDoor} = openHostDoors(current.doorCount, current.carDoor, i)
      mutable gameState = {...current, phase: "decide", pickedDoor: i, openedDoors, remainingDoor}
    }

    container.appendChild(doorEl)
  }

  return container
}
```

```{ojs}
// controlsPanel: instructions plus whichever buttons match the current
// phase — nothing during "pick" (click a door above), Stay/Switch during
// "decide", Play again during "result".
controlsPanel = {
  const state = gameState
  const container = document.createElement("div")
  container.className = "ojs-panel"

  const decide = (choice) => {
    const current = mutable gameState
    const finalDoor = choice === "switch" ? current.remainingDoor : current.pickedDoor
    const won = finalDoor === current.carDoor
    const round = {doorCount: current.doorCount, pickedDoor: current.pickedDoor, carDoor: current.carDoor, decision: choice, won, source: "played"}
    mutable rounds = [...mutable rounds, round]
    mutable gameState = {...current, phase: "result", decision: choice, won}
  }

  if (state.phase === "pick") {
    container.innerHTML = "<p>Pick a door — one hides the car, the rest hide goats.</p>"
  } else if (state.phase === "decide") {
    const msg = document.createElement("p")
    const openedCount = state.openedDoors.length
    msg.innerHTML = `You picked <strong>Door ${state.pickedDoor + 1}</strong>. The host opened ${openedCount} goat door${openedCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}, leaving <strong>Door ${state.remainingDoor + 1}</strong> closed besides yours.`
    container.appendChild(msg)

    const buttonRow = document.createElement("div")
    buttonRow.className = "ojs-row"

    const stayBtn = document.createElement("button")
    stayBtn.className = "btn btn-outline-primary"
    stayBtn.textContent = `Stay with Door ${state.pickedDoor + 1}`
    stayBtn.onclick = () => decide("stay")

    const switchBtn = document.createElement("button")
    switchBtn.className = "btn btn-primary"
    switchBtn.textContent = `Switch to Door ${state.remainingDoor + 1}`
    switchBtn.onclick = () => decide("switch")

    buttonRow.append(stayBtn, switchBtn)
    container.appendChild(buttonRow)
  } else if (state.phase === "result") {
    const msg = document.createElement("p")
    const outcome = state.won ? "🎉 You won the car!" : "🐐 That was a goat."
    msg.innerHTML = `<strong>${outcome}</strong> You chose to <strong>${state.decision}</strong>.`
    container.appendChild(msg)

    const againBtn = document.createElement("button")
    againBtn.className = "btn btn-primary"
    againBtn.textContent = "Play again"
    againBtn.onclick = () => { mutable gameState = newGame(state.doorCount) }
    container.appendChild(againBtn)
  }

  return container
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
stats = {
  const summarize = (source) => {
    let stayWins = 0, stayTotal = 0, switchWins = 0, switchTotal = 0
    for (const round of rounds) {
      if (source !== null && round.source !== source) continue
      if (round.decision === "stay") {
        stayTotal++
        if (round.won) stayWins++
      } else {
        switchTotal++
        if (round.won) switchWins++
      }
    }
    return {stayWins, stayTotal, switchWins, switchTotal}
  }
  return {played: summarize("played"), all: summarize(null)}
}
```

  <strong>Theoretical, at ${doorCount} doors:</strong> stay ${formatPct(1, doorCount)}, switch ${formatPct(doorCount - 1, doorCount)}.
</div>`

```{ojs}
// statsControls: always-visible controls, independent of the game phase —
// resetting stats or running a batch of instant simulated rounds don't
// touch the door board above.
statsControls = {
  const container = document.createElement("div")
  container.className = "ojs-row"

  const makeButton = (label, cls, onClick) => {
    const btn = document.createElement("button")
    btn.className = cls
    btn.textContent = label
    btn.onclick = onClick
    return btn
  }

  const simulate = (n) => {
    const batch = []
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      batch.push(simulateRound(doorCount, i % 2 === 0 ? "stay" : "switch"))
    }
    mutable rounds = [...mutable rounds, ...batch]
  }

  container.append(
    makeButton("Reset stats", "btn btn-outline-secondary", () => { mutable rounds = [] }),
    makeButton("Simulate +100 rounds", "btn btn-outline-primary", () => simulate(100)),
    makeButton("Simulate +1000 rounds", "btn btn-outline-primary", () => simulate(1000))
  )

  return container
}
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Convergence plot"}

```{ojs}
// convergencePlot: running win rate for each strategy, plotted against how
// many times that strategy has been used so far (played and simulated
// rounds combined, in the order they happened) — the classic
// law-of-large-numbers picture, with dashed reference lines at the
// theoretical win rates for the current door count.
convergencePlot = {
  const stayRows = [], switchRows = []
  let stayWins = 0, stayCount = 0, switchWins = 0, switchCount = 0
  for (const round of rounds) {
    if (round.decision === "stay") {
      stayCount++
      if (round.won) stayWins++
      stayRows.push({x: stayCount, y: stayWins / stayCount})
    } else {
      switchCount++
      if (round.won) switchWins++
      switchRows.push({x: switchCount, y: switchWins / switchCount})
    }
  }

  const stayName = "Stay"
  const switchName = "Switch"
  const stayTheoryName = `Theoretical stay (1/${doorCount})`
  const switchTheoryName = `Theoretical switch (${doorCount - 1}/${doorCount})`
  const colorDomain = [stayName, switchName, stayTheoryName, switchTheoryName]
  const colorRange = ["#dc2626", "#16a34a", "#fca5a5", "#86efac"]

  const marks = [
    Plot.ruleY([1 / doorCount], {stroke: () => stayTheoryName, strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.ruleY([(doorCount - 1) / doorCount], {stroke: () => switchTheoryName, strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.lineY(stayRows, {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: () => stayName}),
    Plot.lineY(switchRows, {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: () => switchName})
  ]

  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: 340, height: 300, marginLeft: 46,
    x: {label: "round (within strategy)"},
    y: {label: "win rate", domain: [0, 1]},
    color: {domain: colorDomain, range: colorRange},
    marks
  })
  const legend = Plot.legend({color: {domain: colorDomain, range: colorRange}})

  const container = document.createElement("div")
  container.append(chart, legend)
  return container
}
```

:::

roundHistoryTable = {

  const rows = []

    rows
  })
}

## Why this matters

Your first pick has a $1/N$ chance of hiding the car, for $N$ doors — that never changes, no matter what the host does afterward. What changes is the *other* doors: together they started out holding the remaining $(N-1)/N$ probability, and the host's reveals don't spread that probability back out evenly — they collapse all of it onto the single door left closed, because the host's choice is never random. The host always knows where the car is, and always opens goats. Switching lets you trade your original $1/N$ chance for that door's $(N-1)/N$ chance.

This is why the effect gets more dramatic as $N$ grows: at 3 doors, switching wins $2/3$ of the time versus $1/3$ for staying — a noticeable but not overwhelming edge. Push the slider up to 10 doors and switching wins $9/10$ of the time while staying wins just $1/10$ — the host revealing 8 goats one by one is a lot of information, and all of it piles onto that one remaining door. Run a few thousand simulated rounds at each end of the slider and watch the convergence plot's two lines settle almost immediately onto their theoretical values, while your own manual plays (fewer, so noisier) drift around the same lines.
